claims.claim: 엑셀 텍스트 나누기는 Data 탭의 Text to Columns 로 시작해, 마법사에서 Delimited → 구분 기호 선택 → Destination → Finish 순서로 끝난다(마법사 문서 기준 7단계).
evidence: 마법사 문서 원문 7단계: 1) 나눌 텍스트가 있는 셀 또는 열 선택 2) Data > Text to Columns 3) Convert Text to Columns Wizard 에서 Delimited > Next 4) 데이터의 Delimiters 선택(예: Comma and Space, Data preview 창에서 미리보기) 5) Next 6) 나눈 데이터가 나타날 Destination 선택 7) Finish
도입 원문: "Take text in one or more cells and split it into multiple cells using the Convert Text to Columns Wizard." 같은 문서 끝 'Want more?' 에 'Split text into different columns with functions' 링크

Distribute 문서 Windows 탭 원문: "On the Data tab, in the Data Tools group, select Text to Columns." 그다음 "Follow the instructions in the Convert Text to Columns Wizard to specify how you want to divide the text into separate columns."
Distribute 문서 예시: 'Full Name' 열을 'First Name' 열과 'Last Name' 열 2개로 분할
마법사 문서 Applies To 원문: Excel for Microsoft 365 / Excel 2024 / Excel 2021 / Excel 2019 / Excel 2016 (5개, Mac 표기 없음)

claims.claim: 나눈 결과는 오른쪽 셀을 덮어쓰므로, 시작 전에 오른쪽에 빈 열을 충분히 남겨 두어야 한다(나눌 범위는 행은 몇 개든 되지만 열은 1개만).
evidence: Distribute 문서 Windows 탭 Note 원문: "A range containing a column that you want to split can include any number of rows, but it can include no more than one column. Keep enough blank columns to the right of the selected column to prevent data in any adjacent columns from being overwritten by the data that is to be distributed. If necessary, insert empty columns to contain each of the constituent parts of the distributed data."
Split a cell 문서 Important 원문: "When you split the contents, they will overwrite the contents in the next cell to the right, so make sure to have empty space there."
(2차 보조·공식 아님) 조지아대 재무회계부서 헬프 문서: 새 빈 열을 먼저 삽입하지 않으면 기존 열이 원본 텍스트로 덮어쓰이며, 마지막 단계에서 덮어쓸지 묻는 확인 팝업이 뜬다고 서술(팝업 문구 자체는 원문 미인용)

claims.claim: 같은 '텍스트 나누기'라도 문서·플랫폼마다 메뉴 이름·흐름·적용 버전이 다르게 적혀 있어, 한 흐름으로 뭉뚱그리지 말고 문서별로 귀속해 써야 한다.
evidence: Distribute 문서는 'Windows' / 'Web' 탭 2개. Windows 탭: Data tab > Data Tools group > Text to Columns 후 마법사. Web 탭 원문: "On the Data tab, in the Data Tools group, select Split Text to Columns." → "Select the delimiters that you want to use, and then select Apply." (마법사가 아니라 Apply 흐름)

Split a cell 문서 Note 원문: "Excel for the web doesn't have the Text to Columns Wizard. Instead, you can Split text into different columns with functions." 같은 문서의 단계는 탭 구분 없이 "Select Data > Data Tools > Text to Columns" → 구분 기호 선택 → Apply("Use Custom to split at comma + space")로 서술
Applies To 가 문서마다 다름: 마법사 문서 5개(365·2024·2021·2019·2016) / Distribute 문서 3개(365·2024·2021) / Split a cell 문서 5개(365·2024·2021·2019·2016)
Split a cell 문서 도입: "Excel does not support splitting a single cell like Word tables do." 대신 셀 내용을 인접 셀(열 또는 행)로 나누거나 행·열을 삽입하는 방식

claims.claim: TEXTSPLIT 은 마법사와 같은 일을 수식으로 하는 함수이며, 문서의 Applies To 는 Microsoft 365·365 Mac·2024·2024 Mac 4개뿐이다.
evidence: 원문: "The TEXTSPLIT function works the same as the Text-to-Columns wizard, but in formula form. It allows you to split across columns or down by rows. It is the inverse of the TEXTJOIN function."
Applies To 원문 목록: Excel for Microsoft 365 / Excel for Microsoft 365 for Mac / Excel 2024 / Excel 2024 for Mac (4개). Excel 2021·2019·2016 과 Excel for the web 은 이 목록에 없음
구문 원문: =TEXTSPLIT(text,col_delimiter,[row_delimiter],[ignore_empty], [match_mode], [pad_with]) — 인수 6개, 구문상 대괄호 없음 2개(text·col_delimiter) — 원문 Required 명시는 text 만
기본값 원문: ignore_empty 기본 FALSE(연속 구분 기호가 빈 셀을 만듦), match_mode 기본 0(대소문자 구분, 1 이면 구분 안 함), pad_with 기본 #N/A
Remarks 원문: 구분 기호가 둘 이상이면 배열 상수를 써야 한다. 예) 쉼표와 마침표 모두로 나누려면 =TEXTSPLIT(A1,{",","."})

예시 원문: =TEXTSPLIT(A2, " ") 로 'Dakota Lennon Sanchez'·'To be or not to be' 분할, =TEXTSPLIT(A2,",",";") 로 '1,2,3;4,5,6' 을 2X3 array 로 분할. Example 7 Tip 원문: "To remove the #NA error, use the IFNA function. Or add the pad_with argument." (원문 표기는 '#NA')

claims.claim: 구분 기호가 일정하지 않거나 패턴이 보이면 Flash Fill(Data > Flash Fill 또는 Ctrl+E), 글자 위치로 쪼갤 땐 LEFT·MID·RIGHT·SEARCH·LEN 함수를 대안으로 쓸 수 있다.
evidence: Flash Fill 문서 원문: "Flash Fill automatically fills your data when it senses a pattern. For example, you can use Flash Fill to separate first and last names from a single column, or combine first and last names from two different columns."
Flash Fill 실행 원문: "Data > Flash Fill" 또는 Ctrl+E (Windows·macOS 두 탭 모두에 있음). Applies To 7개: 365 / 2024 / 2024 for Mac / 2021 / 2021 for Mac / 2019 / 2016
Split a cell 문서 원문: "When your text split isn't consistent or you just want Excel to \"figure it out\", you can use Flash Fill."

함수 분할 문서 원문: "You can use the LEFT, MID, RIGHT, SEARCH, and LEN text functions to manipulate strings of text in your data. For example, you can distribute the first, middle, and last names from a single cell into three separate columns." Applies To 9개(365·365 Mac·2024·2024 Mac·2021·2021 Mac·2019·2016·Excel Web App)
함수 분할 문서 Example 1('Jeff Smith', 공백 1개): 이름 =LEFT(A2, SEARCH(" ",A2,1)), 성 =RIGHT(A2,LEN(A2)-SEARCH(" ",A2,1)). 원문 설명상 이름 수식은 공백 위치(5번째)까지 "returns five characters in cell A2, starting from the left"

 Applies To
Excel for Microsoft 365 Excel 2024 Excel 2021 Excel 2019 Excel 2016 
Get help with Copilot
 How do I split text into different columns?
 Learn about the Text Wizard in Excel.
 Help me split text into different columns.
Take text in one or more cells and split it into multiple cells using the Convert Text to Columns Wizard.
Try it!
Select the cell or column that contains the text you want to split.
Select Data > Text to Columns.
In the Convert Text to Columns Wizard, select Delimited > Next.
Select the Delimiters for your data. For example, Comma and Space. You can see a preview of your data in the Data preview window.
Select Next.
Select the Destination in your worksheet which is where you want the split data to appear.
Select Finish.

sources.title: TEXTSPLIT function
sources.body:
TEXTSPLIT function
 Applies To
Excel for Microsoft 365 Excel for Microsoft 365 for Mac Excel 2024 Excel 2024 for Mac 
Release notes
Current Channel
Monthly Enterprise Channel
Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel
Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel (Preview)
Office for Mac
Splits text strings by using column and row delimiters.
The TEXTSPLIT function works the same as the Text-to-Columns wizard, but in formula form. It allows you to split across columns or down by rows. It is the inverse of the TEXTJOIN function. 
Syntax
=TEXTSPLIT(text,col_delimiter,[row_delimiter],[ignore_empty], [match_mode], [pad_with])
The TEXTSPLIT function syntax has the following arguments:
text    The text you want to split. Required. 
col_delimiter    The text that marks the point where to spill the text across columns.
row_delimiter    The text that marks the point where to spill the text down rows. Optional.
ignore_empty    Specify TRUE to ignore consecutive delimiters. Defaults to FALSE, which creates an empty cell. Optional.
match_mode Specify 1 to perform a case-insensitive match. Defaults to 0, which does a case-sensitive match. Optional.
pad_with        The value with which to pad the result. The default is #N/A.
Remarks
If there is more than one delimiter, then an array constant must be used. For example, to split by both a comma, and a period, use =TEXTSPLIT(A1,{",","."}).
Examples
Copy the example data and paste it in cell A1 of a new Excel worksheet. If you need to, you can adjust the column widths to see all the data. 
Example 1
Split a name and a sentence by using a common delimiter.
Data
Dakota Lennon Sanchez
To be or not to be

Example 2

sources.body:
Using Flash Fill in Excel
 Applies To
Excel for Microsoft 365 Excel 2024 Excel 2024 for Mac Excel 2021 Excel 2021 for Mac Excel 2019 Excel 2016 
Get help with Copilot
 Help me use Flash Fill in Excel.
 Explain how to split a column of data based on what I type.
 How should I start flash fill manually?
Flash Fill automatically fills your data when it senses a pattern. For example, you can use Flash Fill to separate first and last names from a single column, or combine first and last names from two different columns.
Windows
macOS
Let's say column A contains first names, column B has last names, and you want to fill column C with first and last names combined. If you establish a pattern by typing the full name in column C, Excel's Flash Fill feature will fill in the rest for you based on the pattern you provide.
Enter the full name in cell C2, and press ENTER.
Start typing the next full name in cell C3. Excel will sense the pattern you provide, and show you a preview of the rest of the column filled in with your combined text.
To accept the preview, press ENTER.
If Flash Fill doesn't generate the preview, it might not be turned on. You can go to Data > Flash Fill to run it manually, or press Ctrl+E. To turn Flash Fill on, go to Tools > Options > Advanced > Editing Options > check the Automatically Flash Fill box.
Let's say column A contains first names, column B has last names, and you want to fill column C with first and last names combined. If you establish a pattern by typing the full name in column C, Excel's Flash Fill feature will fill in the rest for you based on the pattern you provide.
Enter the full name in cell C2, and press ENTER.
Go to Data > Flash Fill, or press Ctrl+E.
Excel will sense the pattern you provided in C2, and fill the cells below.

Split text into different columns with functions
 Applies To
Excel for Microsoft 365 Excel for Microsoft 365 for Mac Excel 2024 Excel 2024 for Mac Excel 2021 Excel 2021 for Mac Excel 2019 Excel 2016 Excel Web App 
Get help with Copilot
 How do I split text into different columns with functions?
 What if I can't use the trim function?
 Explain how to find function.
You can use the LEFT, MID, RIGHT, SEARCH, and LEN text functions to manipulate strings of text in your data. For example, you can distribute the first, middle, and last names from a single cell into three separate columns.
The key to distributing name components with text functions is the position of each character within a text string. The positions of the spaces within the text string are also important because they indicate the beginning or end of name components in a string.
For example, in a cell that contains only a first and last name, the last name begins after the first instance of a space. Some names in your list may contain a middle name, in which case, the last name begins after the second instance of a space.
This article shows you how to extract various components from a variety of name formats using these handy functions. You can also split text into different columns with the Convert Text to Columns Wizard

sources.title: Split a cell in Excel
sources.body:
Split a cell in Excel
 Applies To
Excel for Microsoft 365 Excel 2024 Excel 2021 Excel 2019 Excel 2016 
Get help with Copilot
 How do I split the content from one cell into two or more?
 Show me how split text from one cell into multiple cells.
 Split a cell in Excel for me.
You might want to split a cell into two smaller cells within a single column. Unfortunately, Excel does not support splitting a single cell like Word tables do. 
In Word, a table is a layout tool for arranging text on a page. Cells can be split or merged freely because they don’t represent structured data.
In Excel, a cell is the smallest unit of data. Every cell must live at a specific row and column intersection. Excel worksheets are like graph paper — each square already has a fixed position, so you add more squares instead of cutting one in half. Because of that, Excel cannot split a single cell into multiple cells the way Word can.
Instead, Excel lets you:
Split the contents of a cell into adjacent cells (columns or rows), or
Insert new rows or columns to hold additional data.
See the following screenshots for an example:
Split the content from one cell into two or more cells
Note
Excel for the web doesn't have the Text to Columns Wizard. Instead, you can Split text into different columns with functions.
Select the cell or cells whose contents you want to split. For example,
Important
When you split the contents, they will overwrite the contents in the next cell to the right, so make sure to have empty space there.
Select Data > Data Tools > Text to Columns.
Choose the delimiter or delimiters to define the places where you want to split the cell content, and then select Apply. Use Custom to split at comma + space.
The cell is spit across three columns.
Note
You can transpose columns to rows. After you finish splitting the cell, copy the results then choose Paste Special > Transpose Rows and Columns.
Use Flash Fill to split cells
When your text split isn't consistent or you just want Excel to "figure it out", you can use Flash Fill. This is good when you want to separate names from a single column or combine first and last names from two different columns. 
For an example, see Using Flash Fill in Excel.
Split cell into two or more columns or rows using TEXTSPLIT (Excel on the web)
In Excel on the web, if your data is in one cell and separated by a delimiter (comma, semicolon, line break, etc.) you can use the TEXTSPLIT function.
Enter "Apple, Banana, Cherry" into a cell A1.
In the cell immediately to the right, enter the formula =TEXTSPLIT(A1,,", ") and press Enter.
The result is the column is split into three rows at the delimiter.

sources.title: Splitting Text into Different Columns (University of Georgia F&A knowledge base)
sources.body:
Overview    
You can take text in one column and split it into two or more columns. 
This might be useful if you have a column of query results that has employee first name and last name in the same column. Splitting the data into two columns allows you to filter by either first or last name.
In this article, you will learn the steps to split text in one column into two different columns in an Excel worksheet.
For this example, you will split a column that contains employee names into two separate columns, one for first name and one for last name.
 1. Step 1 
In order to split text into two columns, you will need to insert a new blank column to which you want to move the data. Otherwise, an existing column will be overwritten with the text from the source column.
To insert a column, right-click the column header to the right of the one you want to split.
Example shown here: split the employee names in column C into two columns. To insert a blank column next to column C,   right-click the D column header.
 2. Step 2 
A pop-up menu is displayed.
Click the Insert option.
 3. Step 3 
A new blank column is displayed.
Select the appropriate source column that contains the data you want to split.    
Example shown here:  C column header.
 4. Step 4 
With the source column selected, click the Data tab within the ribbon menu.
 5. Step 5 
Click the Text to Columns...  button.
 6. Step 6 
The Convert Text to Columns Wizard is displayed with a preview of the selected data. From the wizard, choose the type of data that best describes the data you want to split into a different column.
By default, the Delimited option is checked, which means the data in the column you want to split is separated by a type of delimiter, such as a comma.
With the appropriate data type selected, click the Next > button.
 7. Step 7 
Next, select the appropriate delimiter(s) that your data contains, then click the Next > button.  
Example shown here: Accepted the preselected delimiters (Tab and Space) clicked the Next >  button.
 8. Step 8 
Select the data format and appropriate destination column(s) where you will send your data, then click the  Finish  button.
Example shown here: Accepted the preselected Column data format (General ) and the Destination (which is autopopulated based on the cells you selected), clicked the Finish button.
 9. Step 9 
A pop-up window appears asking if you are sure you want to overwrite the data in the selected column.
Click the OK button.
 10. Step 10 
The selected data has been split between the source and destination columns. Adjust the column names as needed
